mr_used: For every nuclide i in every material m at every depletion step t: N_{m,i}(t) >= 0. A depletion/burnup solver applied to a non-negative initial number-density vector must return a non-negative number-density vector (atom concentrations are intensive physical quantities >= 0). CRAM (Chebyshev Rational Approximation Method) approximates exp(A*t)*n0 for the stiff Bateman equations and can return small NEGATIVE number densities, violating the non-negativity invariant.
